title: Answer: a detailed illusionist theory that leaves a hard problem standing

statements.text: Illusionism should be abandoned if it demonstrably fails to account for the phenomena. The test is whether a detailed illusionist theory that fully explained reports, judgments and intuitions would still leave a hard problem on reflection. Dennett adds that insurmountable obstacles to a subpersonal model of all human competences would show why a robot of robots could not be a zombie.

sources.quote: abandoned only if it demonstrably fails to account for phenomena
would we still want to insist, on reflection, that a hard problem remained?
if there are insurmountable obstacles to providing a subpersonal model of all the competences and biases that must be present for an agent to be a ‘zombie’
